Fixed in 4f2de01 and verified on real hardware 2026-07-28 00:07.

Root cause: when a monitor renegotiated resolution mid-run, setup-monitor correctly aborted with exit code 75, but monitor-watcher's reconcile loop then timed out instead of retrying, because start_time was set once before the loop while reap_setup had just cleared setup_pid. setup-monitor therefore never reached its fluxbox restart, so _NET_DESKTOP_GEOMETRY kept a stale value (6720x2160 for an 8000x2160 screen) and xfce4-notifyd placed notifications at +0+0.

Verified by replugging the Odyssey G75F, which reproduced the exact renegotiation (640x480 -> 3440x1440 -> 5120x2160) and the STALE abort, then showed the new 'Setup aborted as stale; waiting for new state to settle (retry 1/3)' path relaunching setup-monitor, which completed with exit code 0. _NET_DESKTOP_GEOMETRY is now 8000x2160 and notifications land correctly.

The nm-applet icon symptom originally filed here has a different cause and is split out as dc-9l7.

Fixed in audio repo commit 0ca9704 plus an edit to ~/.network-handler.d/mute (untracked by any repo).

Root cause: PipeWire has no master volume. Each sink holds its own mute state
and @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ is an alias resolved at use time, so muting the
default sink is undone whenever the default moves - which plugging in a
monitor reliably causes, since the new DisplayPort audio sink becomes default
and is unmuted.

Fix: wpvol gains mute-all/unmute-all, acting on every sink that can make
noise in the room (the machine's speaker plus all HDMI/DisplayPort outputs,
since monitors may have speakers). USB DACs and Bluetooth are left alone as
deliberately-chosen outputs. ~/.network-handler.d/mute now calls these
instead of the single-sink mute/unmute.

Verified end to end: invoking the handler with 'Ocean 23456' unmutes all five
sinks, and with 'L39-Member' mutes all five. Whichever sink becomes default
after a later monitor plug is therefore already muted.

Accepted trade-off: wired headphones are not a separate sink on this
hardware - plugging them in switches the device profile (Speaker ->
Headphones) and reuses the same sink node, so they are muted too. Adam
confirmed he does not use wired headphones.

Also fixed a latent bug in wpvol: getvol() kept only the volume level via
awk '{print $2}', discarding the MUTED marker, so 'getvol | grep -q MUTED'
could never match and MUTE_STATE was always 'no'. Affected only the bar()
display, since mute()/unmute() call wpctl set-mute directly.

Fixed in deef382. A one-shot force_setup flag is set on a stale abort and consumed by the first subsequent settle, so a configuration which settles back to the previously-applied MD5 is re-applied rather than skipped.

Verified by replaying the recorded journal sequences through the decision
logic:
  plain change, no renegotiation              -> 1 setup
  second DRM event, genuinely unchanged       -> 0 setups (no regression)
  stale abort settling back to applied MD5    -> 1 setup (was 0; the bug)
  stale abort then repeated settles           -> 1 setup (no runaway loop)
  stale abort settling to a DIFFERENT config  -> 1 setup

Also verified end to end on the live desktop: running setup-monitor by hand
after the 00:47 skip completed rc=0, restarted fluxbox, and restored correct
behaviour - notification at +7733+2052 (bottom-right of DisplayPort-1, pointer
placed there) and nm-applet icon 32x32 at +7442+2126.

NOT yet verified is the fix firing automatically during a real renegotiating
replug; that needs the hardware event tracked by dc-jzm.

Fixed in 972b6a5: get-layout now returns a wait state for EDID-less DP fallback modes (model-less/Unknown + 0mm, and res=N/A) instead of committing to celtic+external-secondary. 8/8 unit cases pass including two guarding against rejecting genuine small monitors. Real-world verification across a DPMS blank/unblank cycle still pending and tracked under dc-ut8.

Fixed across 972b6a5, a300baa and 2b16827. Root cause: the watcher compared the MD5 of the whole inxi blob, which includes 'res', so a DisplayPort monitor's staged mode negotiation read as repeated reconfigurations during a blank/unblank cycle in which nothing was plugged or unplugged.

Final fix keys change detection on monitor identity (connector + model, resolution deliberately excluded) via the new bin/monitor-identity, shared by monitor-watcher and setup-monitor so their comparisons agree. Resolution can be excluded because layouts are percentage-based and resolved against live xrandr geometry at apply time.

VERIFIED on the real system by forcing DPMS off/on:
  Settled layout after 9s: celtic+ultrawide
  Monitor configuration unchanged (MD5: DisplayPort-1=SAMSUNG Odyssey G75F,eDP=BOE NJ NE135A1M-NY1), skipping setup
Zero setup-monitor launches, against 1 launch + stale abort after a300baa and 2 full relayouts before it.

Note the settle-window increase in a300baa proved insufficient on its own -- the intermediate mode's dwell time is variable (6s in the journal, >9s when tested), so no constant works. It is retained only to guard the first layout selection during a genuine multi-monitor hotplug.

Discovered while testing and split out as dc-wtm: the monitor advertises 3440x1440 as its EDID-preferred mode, so it can settle at the wrong resolution independently of any watcher behaviour.

Saved the physically undocked laptop-only topology as autorandr profile `celtic`.

Verified on the live system:

- `autorandr --detected --skip-options gamma` reports `celtic`.
- `autorandr --current --skip-options gamma` reports `celtic`.
- `bin/test-monitor-watcher-ng` passes all 8 behavioral tests.
- A foreground `setup-monitor --skip-xrandr` run completed in 18.3 seconds, including window layout, Fluxbox restart, panel restart, and system-tray stabilization.

Root cause of the missed 12:20 undock was exactly the absent laptop-only profile: the watcher observed the DRM event and retried for 30 seconds, but autorandr could not match any saved profile, so the desktop postswitch pipeline was never launched.
